name: Heliotrope-Slate
lede: Heliotrope-Slate is a dark, barely purplish grey named for the heliotrope flower, one of the more common named colors in our painting archive.

sections.title: A dark heliotrope
sections.body:
The library records Heliotrope-Slate from the 1912 Ridgway atlas, plate L, hue 65, tone i, carried into the ISCC-NBS system's block 228 in 1955 [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[plumbago-slate]], [[blackish-grey]], [[smoke]] and [[vinaceous-slate]], at 2.6, 3.4, 
In LCH terms it measures lightness 41, chroma 5, hue 305 degrees, a near-neutral the ISCC-NBS system calls "dark purplish gray", close to plain grey and distinct from the [[blue]] or [[violet]] cast its name might suggest, Munsell notation N 4.0 [1]. 6, 3.4, 3.6 and 3.6 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds this color in 255 of 23,781 paintings, 1.07 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 113 [2]. That makes it more common than 61 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 31 of 1,674 paintings, at 1.9 percent of that century's paintings, 2.8 times the expected rate [2]. Inside a painting it most often sits as a mid-tone, in 34 percent of its appearances, by lightness rank [2].

The earliest match in our archive is dated 1400, by Sano di Pietro; that is 512 years before the name's own first record, in 1912, so the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not evidence of the actual paint, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
